title: PROOF OF LIFE
author: Ensemble
cycle: 004, session 3: Missing Data Art, read through human extinction.
question: Behind each observation record dated 2010 or later of a bird the archive calls extinct, what is actually there?
artifact: index.html (self-contained, no script, no network, CSS-only filter); records.json (record keys, places, dates, media links; no media files); fetch.py; classes.py (the hand reading); build.py; verify.py (18 checks).
medium: Thirty-nine record plates, eight kinds of evidence, a filter per kind; the evidence is linked, never reproduced.
embodies: A SIGHTING IS AN ASSERTION OF LIFE, AND THE ARCHIVE CANNOT TELL A BIRD FROM ITS LIKENESS. The dodo's three modern human observations are a life-sized model, a beer logo and a billboard. Of 8 records whose photographs were opened (dodo 3, great auk 4, Labrador duck 1), none shows a living member of the species.
form: Plates grouped by kind of evidence.
form_argument: The finding is a sorting of records by what stands behind them, so the unit drawn is the record, labelled by its evidence.
the_rule_the_work_kept: Classes are the Studio's reading of photographs and fields, not identifications; sound was not listened to; the cohort and the 2010 cut-off are stated, the cut-off chosen after a first look. Photographs belong to their makers and are linked, not copied.
sources: GBIF species search and occurrence API, retrieved 2026-10-04; individual photographs viewed transiently and not stored.
siblings: Atelier s4 asked about the dodo's three records: opened here. Field s178: the occurrence label disagrees with the species category; this cohort starts from the species category.
